title: Closure after a relaxation round
statement: Fix a natural parameter $K_0$, an oracle, a Boolean string $x$, and natural numbers $B,P$. Let $varphi\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, let $j$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a machine state, and let $M:\mathbb{Z}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ satisfy that exactly $j$ of the $K$ cells at positions $B_s+v$ for $v<K$ are unmarked. Suppose $U=K$, $V=T=T_2=Z=0$, $ch\leq 1$, every component of $S$ is at most $B$, and $B_s+K\leq B$, $B_s+K\leq P$, and $K+1\leq B$. Then there is a memory $M'$ such that, starting at label $mathrm{rl0}(\varphi)$ with state $S$, memory $M$, and head position $0$, the machine reaches label $mathrm{cn0}(\varphi)$ with state $S$ except that $ch$ is reset to $0$, memory $M'$, and head position $0$, while its guard holds at every time strictly before arrival. Moreover, $M'$ extends the marked positions of $M$ and agrees with $M$ outside the block of positions $B_s+v$ with $v<K$. For every predicate $Q$ on natural numbers, if $Q$ is preserved by each true step between indices below $K$ and holds at every initially marked index below $K$, then it holds at every index below $K$ marked in $M'$. Also, for all $a,b<K$, if $a$ is marked in $M'$ and the step from $a$ to $b$ is true, then $b$ is marked in $M'$.

replaced:
Let $S$ be a machine state, let $M$ be a memory function, and let $j$ be the number of
unmarked cells among the $K$ cells beginning at base $B_s$. Suppose $U=K$,
$V=T=T_2=Z=0$, $ch\leq 1$, and $S$ satisfies the stated bounds $\mathrm{SBd}(B,P)$. For
either Boolean choice $\varphi$, there is a memory $M'$ such that the machine reaches,
while maintaining its guard, the configuration at label $\mathrm{cn0}(\varphi)$ with
state $S$ except that $ch$ is reset to $0$, memory $M'$, and head position $0$, starting
from label $\mathrm{rl0}(\varphi)$ with state $S$, memory $M$, and head position $0$.
Moreover, every cell marked in $M$ remains marked in $M'$, cells outside the block
$\{B_s+v:v<K\}$ are unchanged, and the marked cells in that block are closed under
reachability from initially marked cells: for every predicate $Q$ on natural numbers, if
$Q$ is preserved by each true step relation within the block and holds at every
initially marked index, then it holds at every index marked in $M'$. In addition, if
$a,b<K$, the cell at index $a$ is marked in $M'$, and the step relation from $a$ to $b$
is true, then the cell at index $b$ is marked in $M'$.
